headline: Deadly US Heat Dome Extends Through Monday as PDS Red Flag Warnings Ignite Across Pacific Northwest; Spain–France Wildfire Smoke Blankets Millions
overview: August 1 opens with a convergence of extreme heat, fire, and flooding hazards across multiple continents. The historic US heat dome — now in its third week — continues to drive 110–120°F Extreme Heat Warnings from Arizona to Montana through Monday, while a Particularly Dangerous Situation (PDS) Red Flag Warning from a cold front sweeping the Pacific Northwest threatens explosive fire spread across Oregon, Washington, and Idaho. Simultaneously, the Spain–France wildfire crisis has broadened into a major air quality emergency, with Copernicus data showing millions of Europeans now exposed to PM2.5 concentrations far above safe limits.

events.title: US Heat Dome Persists — Extreme Heat Warnings From Arizona to Montana Through Monday
events.location: Arizona, California, Nevada, Utah, Montana, USA
events.summary: A sprawling and persistent heat dome continues to drive life-threatening temperatures across the American West, with NWS Extreme Heat Warnings active across dozens of zones from Phoenix (110–117°F) and the Coachella Valley/Yuma corridor (112–120°F) to Death Valley, the Mojave Desert, and now much of Montana (100–110°F) through Monday evening. Overnight low temperatures in the 70s–90s are offering little to no relief, dramatically increasing the risk of heat-related illness and death. The heat dome is now in its third consecutive week and has broken or tied dozens of all-time records across the Southwest.

events.title: Spain–France Wildfire Crisis: Copernicus Warns Millions Exposed to Dangerous Air Quality
events.location: Ávila, Castilla y León, Spain; Gironde, France; Western Europe
events.summary: The catastrophic wildfire complex burning across Spain and France — already the largest in Spanish recorded history at over 140,000 hectares — has now escalated into a major transboundary air quality emergency. Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) forecast data shows PM2.5 fine particulate levels in Bordeaux reaching nearly five times the safe daily limit, with millions across southwestern Europe exposed to extremely poor air quality through at least August 2. A new World Weather Attribution analysis released this week directly links climate change to the compounding fire weather drivers behind the 2026 Spain–France wildfire season.

articles.title: Extreme wildfires in western Europe expose millions to dangerous air pollution levels

events.title: Pacific Northwest Wildfire Crisis Escalates — PDS Red Flag Warnings as Cold Front Drives Explosive Conditions
events.summary: A dry cold front sweeping across the Pacific Northwest on August 1 has triggered Particularly Dangerous Situation (PDS) Red Flag Warnings across the Okanogan Valley, Colville Reservation, Waterville Plateau, and Columbia Basin of Washington, along with extensive Red Flag Warnings across central Oregon, north-central Idaho, and much of Montana — creating ideal conditions for explosive, erratic fire behavior. Oregon's Rowe Creek Complex, the state's largest active fire complex, has now reached 199,047 acres at just 31% containment after igniting July 15, while lightning-sparked new ignitions are reported across Central Oregon. Wind gusts of 25–50 mph combined with relative humidities as low as 10–20% are expected to rapidly spread any new or existing fires through the evening.

articles.title: Some Central Oregon wildfires have been 100% contained. See which ones remain
Why Oregon's wildfires have run wild during 2026 season

events.title: Earth-Directed CME Triggers G1–G2 Geomagnetic Storm Forecast for August 2
events.summary: A long-duration M1.9 solar flare from Active Region 4492 coincided with a filament eruption near N20W67 on July 31, producing an eruptive sequence associated with an Earth-directed partial-halo coronal mass ejection (CME). Space weather forecasters at NOAA have issued a G1–G2 (Minor to Moderate) geomagnetic storm watch for August 2, with aurora potentially visible across 10 or more US states. While G1–G2 storms rarely cause significant infrastructure damage, they can disrupt HF radio communications, cause minor fluctuations in power grids, and trigger vivid aurora displays at mid-latitudes.

articles.title: Long-duration M1.9 flare produces Earth-directed CME, G1-G2 geomagnetic storm conditions forecast for August 2

events.title: Nueces River Reaches Major Flood Stage in South Texas — Fatality Reported
events.location: Live Oak and McMullen Counties, South Texas, USA
events.summary: The Nueces River is in major flood stage across South Texas, with NWS Corpus Christi issuing Flood Warnings for Live Oak and McMullen Counties as the river crested near Three Rivers at approximately 39.2 feet — more than 14 feet above the 25-foot flood stage threshold. A person was reported swept away and killed in the Nueces River near Uvalde, and local officials have been preparing communities for potential inundation of low-lying subdivisions. The flood event follows a series of heavy rainfall episodes across South and Central Texas and is expected to recede slowly through the coming days.

articles.title: Officials prepare Texas communities for potential flooding

events.title: Multi-Day Flood Watch Issued for Florida Gulf Coast — Tropical Moisture Threat
events.location: Big Bend and Panhandle Florida (Bay, Gulf, Franklin, Wakulla, Taylor, Hernando, Citrus, Levy Counties), USA
events.summary: NWS Tampa Bay and Tallahassee have issued multi-day Flood Watches covering a broad swath of Florida's Gulf Coast — from the Panhandle through the Big Bend region — valid from August 1 through August 3, driven by persistent tropical moisture and slow-moving thunderstorm complexes. Excessive runoff threatens rivers, creeks, and low-lying areas, with forecasters warning that repeated rounds of heavy rainfall could produce localized flooding lasting several days. The Atlantic hurricane season remains quiet for now, but enhanced tropical moisture continues to funnel heavy rainfall into the Florida Gulf Coast region.

articles.title: Hurricane season update includes tropical waves, stormy Florida

events.title: Kīlauea Episode 52 — Lava Fountaining Continues at Halemaʻumaʻu Crater
events.location: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, Big Island, Hawaiʻi, USA
events.summary: Kīlauea's ongoing Episode 52 eruption continues at Halemaʻumaʻu Crater within the summit caldera, with lava fountaining maintaining active activity as of August 1. The eruption remains confined to the crater and poses no immediate threat to populated areas, though volcanic gas (SO₂) emissions continue and may affect air quality downwind. The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO) continues to monitor the eruption closely; no significant escalation from prior days has been reported.
